svg.title: Grand Aurora: Tenant Isolation, deco drawing
svg.desc: Fictional AWS architecture. Identity lines show browser-carried credentials, not Cognito initiating calls into the APIs. Each API validates issuer, audience, expiry and scopes. VPC Link integrations and internal ALBs remain in their own account/region. The app derives the subject from verified identity, checks selected-hotel membership and assigned-cell policy, and sets tenant context locally within a transaction. A client-supplied tenant ID is a selection, not evidence of entitlement. Pooled PostgreSQL isolation assumes non-owner/non-BYPASSRLS roles, forced row policies, safe transaction pooling and tests covering raw SQL, background workers and administrative paths. The picture does not prove those controls. Separate enterprise credentials/database/account reduce shared-data-plane exposure; the app still rejects other tenants. Identity federation, revocation, privileged operations and complete networking are not implementation artifacts here. This is a focused authored view of the overview’s cell aggregates. Hotel staff to Federated sign-in; Federated sign-in to Shared JWT API; Federated sign-in to Enterprise JWT API; Shared JWT API to Shared VPC Link; Shared VPC Link to Internal shared ALB; Internal shared ALB to Membership and RLS; Membership and RLS to Shared tenant records; Enterprise JWT API to Dedicated VPC Link; Dedicated VPC Link to Internal tenant ALB; Internal tenant ALB to Enterprise allowlist; Enterprise allowlist to Enterprise records. Boundary labels distinguish accounts, regions, VPCs, AZs, subnets and logical groups. These annotations do not verify deployed isolation or permissions.

g.title: Browser authenticates with the federated user pool; MFA and federation must be configured.
Browser presents access token; API validates issuer, audience, expiry and required scopes using cached keys.
Same issuer may serve dedicated tenants, but this API has its own audience and cell authorization policy.
Authorized HTTP integration uses a VPC Link in the same account and region as its load balancer.
Private integration reaches the internal ALB; no direct public app endpoint.
App derives subject from verified identity and validates selected hotel membership.
Server-validated tenant context is transaction-local; non-owner database role and forced RLS enforce row policies.
Dedicated cell has its own same-account private integration.
Private load balancer stays inside the enterprise account.
App rejects valid tokens for tenants not assigned to this cell.
Separate credentials and database; no pooled database route is authorized.
